body:
Substantive self-review under ADR 0004, not independent human approval. Reviewed exact head fb15d2d72dbc18a972cf9b663f168debbbe87856 against base 9e3210c0dbbd18464ad4d3e3aac6c88faaa8e2a0.

Correctness: exact substring prefilters replace only escaped case-sensitive literal regexes. Unicode-folded literals retain the original regex engine. File-level rejection is a necessary condition only; accepted candidates retain the original line matcher and anchors/flags/errors. UTF-8, file/line limits, rule scoping, diagnostic limits and failure handling precede or remain outside the optimization. No rules, manifests, public interfaces, CI, budgets, result caches or unsafe code changed. OnceLock retains a compiled proof only inside the per-scan matcher, not results across scans. Lazy linear proofs and the 4096 estimated-line-visit threshold affect optimization effort only.

Measured selection: eager Trial C was rejected after all-pack single-file startup regressed about 5%. Trial D removes eager setup. Same-host 31-pair selected run: 1001-file corpus 32.249 -> 26.028 ms (1.239x); large repository 58.742 -> 36.987 ms (1.588x); all-pack repository 428.332 -> 355.564 ms (1.205x); actual Rust-source corpus under three baseline packs 30.281 -> 24.531 ms (1.234x). Startup follow-up with 101 pairs includes no change in its intervals: all-pack startup 43.433 -> 43.843 ms, paired interval 0.987-1.018x. AST/TypeScript also show no clear change. Shared-host load was high; no universal speedup or zero-regression guarantee is asserted.

Verification: 331 workspace Rust tests, 31 native differential cases plus 2 real external cases, seven harness tests, unchanged six release budgets, and all nine exact-head CI statuses pass, including native Linux/macOS/Windows CLI/package acceptance. Comparison preserves findings, errors, coverage and exits, normalizing coverage time and only AST's random scratch nonce. Prior and selected raw outputs are preserved on the assigned worker; final selected reports/task closure will land as a documentation-only follow-up after the code merge. All required checks have passed; no unresolved code defect was found in this review.
